message.content:
Below are two ways to launch a **Google Cloud Compute Engine** instance that has an **NVIDIA RTX A6000** GPU and runs **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**.

> ⚠️ **Important**  
> * Google Cloud does **not** use the “EC2” terminology – that’s Amazon Web Services.  
> * You must have a Google Cloud project with billing enabled, the Compute Engine API turned on, and the **GPU quota** for your region satisfied.  
> * The GPU must be attached to a **supported machine type** (e.g., `n1-standard-8`, `n1-highmem-8`, `n1-highcpu-8`, etc.).  
> * The GPU must be in a zone that supports it (e.g., `us-central1-a`, `us-east1-b`, `europe-west4-a`, …).  

---

## 1. Using the `gcloud` CLI

```bash
# Set variables
PROJECT="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"          # pick a zone that supports RTX A6000
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"

# Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
    --project="$PROJECT" \
    --zone="$ZONE" \
    --machine-type="n1-standard-8" \
    --accelerator="type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1" \
    --image-family="ubuntu-2004-lts" \
    --image-project="ubuntu-os-cloud" \
    --boot-disk-size="100GB" \
    --boot-disk-type="pd-ssd" \
    --maintenance-policy="TERMINATE" \
    --restart-on-failure \
    --scopes="https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform" \
    --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh   # optional: run a script at boot
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU & RAM allocation. `n1-standard-8` gives 8 vCPUs & 30 GB RAM. |
| `--accelerator` | Attaches the GPU. `type=nvidia-tesla-a6000` is the RTX A6000. |
| `--image-family` / `--image-project` | Boots from the latest Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image. |
| `--boot-disk-size` / `--boot-disk-type` | SSD boot disk of 100 GB. |
| `--maintenance-policy` | `TERMINATE` means the VM will be stopped if the host is rebooted. |
| `--restart-on-failure` | Auto‑restarts the VM if it crashes. |
| `--scopes` | Grants full Cloud Platform access (adjust as needed). |
| `--metadata-from-file startup-script` | Optional: run a shell script at first boot. |

> **Tip:** If you need a different machine type (e.g., more memory), replace `n1-standard-8` with `n1-highmem-8` or `n1-highcpu-8`. Just make sure the chosen type is supported in your zone.

---

## 2. Using the REST API (JSON)

If you prefer to call the Compute Engine API directly (e.g., from a script or a CI/CD pipeline), you can POST a JSON payload to the `instances.insert` endpoint.

```bash
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/instances
Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN>
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu",
  "machineType": "projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "scheduling": {
    "preemptible": false,
    "automaticRestart": true,
    "onHostMaintenance": "TERMINATE"
  },
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\napt-get update\napt-get install -y build-essential"
      }
    ]
  },
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ]
}
```

### Replace placeholders

| Placeholder | What to put |
|-------------|-------------|
| `{project}` | Your GCP project ID |
| `{zone}` | Zone that supports RTX A6000 (e.g., `us-central1-a`) |
| `<YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN>` | OAuth 2.0 token with `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/compute` scope |

> **Note:** The `acceleratorType` URI uses the same project/zone pattern as the machine type. The `sourceImage` points to the Ubuntu 20.04 LTS family.

---

## Quick Checklist Before Running

1. **Enable Compute Engine API**  
   ```bash
   gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com
   ```

2. **Verify GPU Quota**  
   ```bash
   gcloud compute accelerator-types list --project=$PROJECT --filter="zone:$ZONE"
   ```

3. **Create a Service Account (if using REST)**  
   ```bash
   gcloud iam service-accounts create compute-sa \
       --display-name="Compute Engine Service Account"
   gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding $PROJECT \
       --member="serviceAccount:compute-sa@$PROJECT.iam.gserviceaccount.com" \
       --role="roles/compute.admin"
   ```

4. **Generate OAuth Token**  
   ```bash
   gcloud auth application-default print-access-token
   ```

5. **Run the command** (CLI or REST) and wait for the instance to appear in the console.

---

### Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Likely Cause | Fix |
|---------|--------------|-----|
| `ERROR: (gcloud.compute.instances.create) Resource exhausted: No available GPUs in zone` | GPU quota exceeded or zone doesn’t support RTX A6000 | Request a quota increase or choose another zone. |
| `ERROR: (gcloud.compute.instances.create) Resource exhausted: No available machine types` | Machine type not supported in zone | Pick a supported type (`n1-standard-8`, `n1-highmem-8`, etc.) |
| `ERROR: (gcloud.compute.instances.create) Resource exhausted: No available disks` | SSD quota reached | Increase SSD quota or reduce disk size. |
| `ERROR: (gcloud.compute.instances.create) Resource exhausted: No available CPUs` | CPU quota reached | Request a higher CPU quota or use a smaller machine type. |

---

## Wrap‑Up

- **CLI** is the quickest way if you’re already using `gcloud`.  
- **REST** gives you fine‑grained control and is handy for automation.  
- Always double‑check quotas and zone compatibility before launching.  

Happy GPU computing! 🚀
